I found three things that must change before this lands, so the verdict is **fix**. The work meets all four numbered asks plus the docs and tests, and the review is written to `leaks/review.md`.

**What must change:**
1. **The leak report will get slow.** `Servex/leaks.mjs`'s `pair()` compares every start line with every other line. At about 55k sampled start lines a day, a run will take minutes within a day or two. The fix is to look lines up by pid.
2. **A Servex restart leaves start lines with no end line.** Lineage forgets what it was tracking, and SpawnLog's exit listeners are lost. So a process that dies during the restart, or a dev server that lives through it, never gets an end line. Each one will show up as "gone, end missed" in every report. Either rebuild the open list when Servex boots, or name this limit in the doc.
3. **One sentence in `Servex/doc/processes.md` is false.** It says the leak report still shows detached grandchildren that have no log line. `leaks.mjs` only reads log lines, so it can't.

**Notes, nothing broken:**
- The test wrote a junk start line for pid 101 into a real task log. It will be the "gone" row in every future report unless someone appends a matching end line.
- About 80 lines a minute go into session logs that are committed to git. The cap is per agent, so nothing limits the total.
- The new guard in `Lifecycle.kill()` lets the kill through when it has no process table loaded, rather than refusing it.
- One branch of the new "is this Chrome ours" pattern (a `lew42` profile folder) matches no profile any code launches. It only makes the set of browsers the sweep may close wider.
- Smaller items are in the file: a possible duplicate end line in `Browser.mjs`, a stray indent in `Processes.js`, files changed outside the brief's list (all justified close paths), and `leaks.mjs` missing from the Servex readme's index.

I re-ran the Lineage, leaks, SpawnLog and processes tests in the worktree and they all pass. The syntax check (`node --check`) is clean on all 8 changed source files. The landing note says the Gate-loud, closeout and Crumbs tests also pass; I didn't re-run those. I made no code edits.
